title: Across roughly 19 open-source business tools surveyed, none keeps an immutable user-attributed log by default
content:
This is the strongest general claim in the lead corpus, and it is stated as a survey result rather than an intuition: across roughly 19 open-source business tools examined, not one keeps an immutable, user-attributed, append-only log by default, and in the cases where an audit trail does exist the vendor charges enterprise money for it. The claim is about defaults and packaging, not about theoretical capability.

It is attached to the 20 leads that have no single named tool because they assemble a stack per client. For that cohort a tool-specific pitch is unavailable by construction, so the universal finding *is* the pitch: whatever the client is running, the record layer is missing or paywalled, and Powerhouse supplies it on infrastructure the client owns. The sovereignty argument and the audit argument arrive together rather than as separate sells.

Because the claim is falsifiable per tool, it is also the claim in this corpus most exposed to drift. Any one vendor shipping a free append-only log removes the argument for that tool without touching the other eighteen, so the survey is a maintained asset rather than a fixed fact. Treating it as evidence with an expiry date is the honest way to keep using it.

description: Where an audit trail exists at all, the vendor charges enterprise money for it — which makes the record layer a sellable gap running on infrastructure the client already owns.
